commons.title: Drumming Sato.jpg
commons.description: The Sato drum is a striking and formidable twin drum, reaching an impressive height of at least 7 feet. With its singular, resonant face, this remarkable instrument is celebrated for both its deep cultural significance and its status as a treasured symbol among the Ogu people of Badagry, Lagos, Nigeria. Renowned for its rich, commanding sound and exceptional craftsmanship, the Sato drum serves as a central feature in traditional rituals, ceremonies, and community celebrations, embodying the heart and soul of the Ogu people's heritage.
commons.editorial_reason: The caption specifically identifies the Ogu people, and the image visibly shows their traditional drumming and ceremonial dance attire.

commons.title: The Zangbeto.jpg
commons.description: The Zangbeto(s), meaning, the night watchman guards the communities of the Ogu people every night. Helping to keep the people and their properties in safety. They are not regarded as deities, but as soldiers  during wartimes or as police of the king.
commons.editorial_reason: The caption specifically identifies the Ogu people, and the image visibly shows a Zangbeto community guardian costume associated with their cultural practice.
